units.he: ראש השנה הוא יום ראשון לבריאה, בחי' זה היום תחלת מעשיך, ובכל שנה חוזר הדבר למציאותו הראשון. והעלום נברא בלשון הקודש שהיא בחי' חוה אשה בחי' מלכות עש"כ בכל ר"ה עוסקין ישראל בבנין המלכות שהואבחי' שלימות לשון הקודש, וכמו שבתחלת הבריאה של חועצמה נאמר ויפל ה' א' תרדימה שהיא בחי' תרגום כמבפ"נ כמ וכן בכל שנה צריכין להמשיך בחי' זו להעלות הטוב שבתרגום ללשון הקודש, וכמו שאז בא הנחש שהוא בחי' כלליות הרע של שבעים אומות ופיתה לחוה וכו' כמובפ"נ וכמו כן בכל ר"ה מתעורר הנחש ר"ל וכל השרים של האומות לקטרג על ישראל ולהפריד היחוד ח"ו כמובא בזוה"ק והשי"ת חמל עלינו וציוה עלינו לתקוע בשופר לעורר זכותו של יעקב כמבואר בזוה"ק, כי יעקב זכה להכניע הנחש והיה בבית לבן הארמי ובירר הטוב שבתרגום והעלה אותו ללה"ק כמובפ"נ, וזה שמבואר בכוונת הנסירה של ר"ה מענין ויפל ה' א' תרדימה על האדם שהא גימט' תרגום, וענין ויבן ה' א' את הצלע וכו' כיכל תיקונים אלו צריכין להמשיך בכל ר"ה כנ"ל, וזה בחי' המלך הקדוש שאומרין אז שזה בחי לשון הקודש כי מלכות פה. וזה בחי' הד' ובכן שאומרין אז ובכן יתקדש הוא נגד בחי' קודש ובכן תן פחדך וכו' כי עיקר עשיה ותיקון של לשון הקודש הוא ע"י היראה כמבפ"נ ובכן תן כבוד הוא כי שלימות לשון הקודש הוא בבחי' כבוד כמבפ"נ ובכן צדיקים הוא נגד בחי'תיקון הברית התלוי בשלימות לה"ק כמבפ"נ כי צדיק הוא מאן דנטיר ברית, וזהו בחי' צדיק וצדק המבואר בכוונות צדיק הוא בחי' תיקון הברית כנ"ל צדק היא בחי' מלכותא קדישא בחי' לשון קודש בחי' צדק תדברון וכמבואר במ"א, וזה ג"כ בחי' ציון וירושלים כידוע, וע"כ מתפללין תיכף ועלתה תקפץ פיה וכו' היינ ושיפול הרע של כל השבעים לשון ויהיו בבחי' פה להם ולא ידברו המבפ"נ, וזה כי תעביר ממשלת זדון מן הארץ בחי' הנחש מלכות דסט"א. ותמלוך אתה ה' מהרה לבדך וכו' בהר ציון וכו' ובירושלים וכו', וזה בחי' מצות תקיעת שופר שהיא בחי' התעוררות השינה כמובא היינו כי שינה ותרדימה היא בחי' תרגום וצריכין לעורר מהשינה היינו להעלות הטוב שבתרגום ללשון הקודש שזה עיקר שלימות לה"ק ועי"ז מביאין הארה והתנוצצות לכל האותיות של מעשה בראשית המלובשין בכל דבר שזה תלוי רק בהאדם הבעל בחירה ע"י שמעלה הטוב שבתרגום ללה"ק כמבפ"נ, וע"כ כל ברואי עולם היו מצפין על בריאת אדם הראשון ווהוא קרא לכולם שמות בלה"ק כמובא במ"א, והארה הזאת שמביאין בהאותיות הנ"ל היא ג"כ בחי' התעוררות השינה שזה בחי' בקרב שנים חייהו ופירש"י עוררהו המבפ"נ. ומחמת שכ"ז תלוי ביראה ובתיקון השגגות ויראה תלוי באודנין בבחי' ה' שמעתי שמעך יראתי ע"כ תוקעין בשופר שעי"ז נתעורר יראה כ"ש היתקע שופר בעיר ועם לא יחרדו, גם עי"ז נתעורר הלב לתשובה לתקן אפילו השגגות שהם מבחי' תרגום ומכש"כ על הזדונות שהם מבחי' הרע הגמור של השבעים לשון וע"י כל זה מעלין הטוב שבתרגום ומשלימין את הלה"ק, וע"כ מברכין לשמוע קול שו לשמוע דייקא כי יראה תליא באודנין גם תקיעת שופר הוא זכר למתן תורה שהיה בקול שופר ואז זכו ישראל ליראה גדולה מאחר שכולם שמעו בעצמם מפי הקב"ה כ"ש השמע עם קול אלהים חיים מדבר וכו', וע"כ נקרא שופר כמבואר בזוה"ק שהוא מלשון שפר קדמי וכן מלכי ישפר עלך וכן דרשו רז"ל שפרו מעשיכם שהוא לשון תרגום כי עי"ז מעלין הטוב שבתרגום כנ"ל וזה אשרי העם יודעי תרועה ה' באור פניך יהלכון כי עי"ז זוכין לפנים מאירות כמבפ"נ וע"כ אשרי הזוכה לבוא לצדיק אמיתי על ר"ה ולהסתכל אז בפניו המאירות, ומכש"כ אז זוכין לשמוע מפיו איזה דבר תורה שעי"ז מקבל מפיו הדיבור של לה"ק בשלימות, ויכול לזכות עי"ז לכל טוב לבטל מעצמו הרע של כל האומות ולזכות לבחי' רוח הקודש ולפנים מאירות ולכל המבפ"נ, וזה בחינת התאדמות פני התוקע כי נמשך עליו בחי' פנים מאירו כנ"ל:
units.en:
Rosh HaShanah is the first day of creation, and on every Rosh HaShanah the matter returns to its primal state. This is the dimension of "This day is the beginning of Your works."

The world was created in the Holy Tongue (Lashon HaKodesh), which is the dimension of Chava (Eve) — woman — Malchus. Therefore on every Rosh HaShanah Israel engage in building Malchus — the dimension of the completeness of the Holy Tongue.

Just as at the beginning of the creation of Chava herself it is written: "and G-d cast a deep sleep" — the dimension of Targum (translation/earthly speech), as explained in the main text — so every year one must draw this dimension to elevate the good within Targum into the Holy Tongue.

And just as the serpent came and enticed Chava — the serpent being the dimension of the totality of evil of the seventy nations — so every Rosh HaShanah the serpent awakens, may G-d protect us, and all the princes of the nations accuse Israel and seek to sever the sacred union, heaven forbid, as brought in the holy Zohar.

Therefore G-d, Yisburach, in His compassion for us, commanded us to sound the Shofar — to awaken the merit of Yaakov, as explained in the holy Zohar. For Yaakov merited to humble the serpent and was in the house of Lavan the Aramean, and clarified the good within Targum and elevated it to the Holy Tongue, as explained in the main text.

This is what is explained in the Kavanos concerning the separation on Rosh HaShanah, involving "And G-d cast a deep sleep upon the man," which has the numerical value of Targum, and concerning "And G-d built the rib," etc. For all these rectifications must be drawn down on every Rosh HaShanah, as above.

This is the dimension of "המלך הקדוש," which one says at that time, for it is the dimension of the Holy Tongue, since Malchus is the mouth.

This is the dimension of the four ובכן prayers recited at that time. "ובכן יתקדש" corresponds to the dimension of holiness. "ובכן תן פחדך" corresponds to awe, for the principal formation and rectification of the Holy Tongue is through awe, as explained in the main text. "ובכן תן כבוד" corresponds to honor, for the completeness of the Holy Tongue is in the dimension of honor, as explained in the main text.

"ובכן צדיקים" corresponds to the dimension of rectifying the covenant, which depends upon the completeness of the Holy Tongue, as explained in the main text, for the Tzadik is one who guards the covenant.

This is the dimension of Tzadik and Tzedek explained in the Kavanos. Tzadik is the dimension of rectifying the covenant, as above. Tzedek is the dimension of holy Malchus, the dimension of the Holy Tongue, in the dimension of "You shall speak righteousness," as explained elsewhere. This is also the dimension of Tzion and Yerushalayim, as is known.

Therefore one immediately prays, "And iniquity shall shut its mouth," etc. That is, the evil of all seventy tongues should fall, so that they should be in the dimension of "They have mouths but cannot speak," as explained in the main text.

This is "For You shall remove the dominion of wickedness from the earth," the dimension of the serpent and the kingship of the Other Side. "And may You, G-d, speedily reign alone," etc., "on Mount Tzion," etc., "and in Yerushalayim," etc.

This is the dimension of the mitzvah of Shofar-sounding, which is the dimension of awakening from sleep, as is brought. For sleep and deep sleep are the dimension of Targum. One must awaken from the sleep — elevating the good within Targum to the Holy Tongue. This is the principal completeness of the Holy Tongue.

Through this one brings illumination and sparkling to all the letters of the act of creation that are clothed within everything. This depends solely upon the human being who possesses free choice, through elevating the good within Targum to the Holy Tongue, as explained in the main text.

Therefore all created beings were awaiting the creation of Adam HaRishon, and he called them all by names in the Holy Tongue, as brought elsewhere.

This illumination brought to the letters mentioned above is also the dimension of awakening from sleep, the dimension of "In the midst of the years, give it life," which Rashi explains as "Awaken it," as explained in the main text.

Because all this depends upon awe and the rectification of inadvertent transgressions, and awe depends upon the ears, in the dimension of "G-d, I heard Your report, I was awed," one therefore sounds the Shofar, through which awe is awakened, as it is written, "Will the Shofar be sounded in the city and the people not tremble?"

Through this the heart is also awakened to repentance, to rectify even inadvertent transgressions, which are of the dimension of Targum, and all the more so deliberate transgressions, which are of the dimension of the complete evil of the seventy tongues. Through all this one elevates the good within Targum and brings the Holy Tongue to completeness.

Therefore one blesses "to hear the sound of the Shofar" — specifically "to hear," for awe depends upon the ears.

Shofar-sounding is also a remembrance of the Giving of the Torah, which took place with the sound of the Shofar. Israel then merited great awe, since they all heard for themselves from the mouth of the Blessed Holy One, as it is written, "Has any people heard the voice of the living G-d speaking," etc.

Therefore it is called Shofar, as explained in the holy Zohar, from the expression "שפר קדמי," and likewise "May my counsel be pleasing to you." Our Sages, z"l, also expounded "Improve your deeds," which is an expression in Targum, for through this one elevates the good within Targum, as explained above.

And this is: "fortunate is the people who know the Teruah; G-d, in the light of Your face they shall walk" — for through this one merits an illuminated face, as explained in the main text.

And therefore fortunate is one who merits to come to the true Tzadik on Rosh HaShanah and to gaze upon his illuminated face — and all the more to merit hearing from his mouth some Torah teaching — through which one receives from him the speech of the Holy Tongue in completeness.

Through this one can merit every good, nullifying within oneself the evil of all the nations and meriting the dimension of the Holy Spirit, an illuminated face, and all that is explained in the main text.

This is the dimension of the reddening of the Shofar-blower's face, for the dimension of an illuminated face is drawn upon him, as explained above.

history.earlier_supplied_English:
On Rosh HaShanah We Engage in Building the Holy Kingdom Through Holy Speech

Rosh HaShanah is the first day of creation, and on every Rosh HaShanah the matter returns to its primal state.

qualifications.text: The source says Rosh HaShanah is the first day of creation and that creation returns to its original state annually. It does not specify the creation of Adam in the opening sentence; Adam appears later as the free-willed human being awaited by the created beings.

The source associates the Holy Tongue with Chava, woman and Malchus, while deep sleep represents Targum. It distinguishes extracting the good from Targum from subduing the evil of the seventy nations and their accusing powers.

The source associates תרדימה with תרגום through gematria, but the literal printed תרדימה has a numerical value of 659, whereas תרגום has 649. The shorter form תרדמה would have 649, but that is contextual information only; the supplied Hebrew is neither corrected nor claimed to reproduce a verified original printing.

The four ובכן prayers are linked respectively to holiness, awe, honor and covenantal rectification. The covenant and holy kingship are further distinguished as Tzadik and Tzedek, with Tzion and Yerushalayim subsequently associated with them.

The source attributes illumination of the letters clothed in created things to human free choice, after elevating the good within Targum. It connects Adam's naming of creatures in the Holy Tongue to the subsequent awakening of these letters.

The printed blessing ends לשמוע קול שו, with the final Shofar word clipped. The English reads it contextually as the blessing over hearing the Shofar, supported by the immediately surrounding discussion, without changing the source or claiming an original printed correction.

The source connects the Shofar's sound to awe through hearing, repentance for inadvertent and deliberate transgressions, the Giving of the Torah and Targum expressions for improvement. The illuminating effect upon the Tzadik's face and the Shofar-blower's reddened face are separate final correspondences.
The current English follows the Hebrew shown here. Earlier supplied English is kept separately for comparison.

units.he: וזה בחי' הג' ספרים שנפתחין בר"ה ספרים דייקא כי ספר הוא לזכרון שהוא בכח המדמה בחי' תרגום כמבפ"נ וע"כ צדיקים גמורים שזכו להעלות גם הטוב שבתרגום ללה,ק ואין להרע שום אחיזה בהם ע"כ בוודאי נכתבין לאלתר לחיים ורשעים גמורים שהם מבחי' הרע הגמור של שבעים לשון והם רוצים להתגבר ולינק גם כן מן הקדושה ח"ו ע"י הרע שבתרגום אך הקדושה מתגברת ומפלת אותם ע"י בחי' השלהובא דאשא המבפ"נ וע"כ נכתבין לאלתר למיתה ר"ל, בינונים הם אותם שהם מבחי' טוב ורע בחי' תרגום ולא זכו עדיין להעלות הטוב שבתרגום ולהפיל הרע שבו ע"כ תלויים ועומדים עד יו"כ כי ע"י התשובה של עשי"ת זוכין לתקן את הלשון תרגום ג"כ עד שגם הם נכתבין לחיים, וזה בחי' תקיעה תרועה תקיעה, תקיעה שלפינה הוא כנגד בחי' הדיבור של לה"ק הבא מלמעלה שעדיין חסר תיקון כי צריכין להעלות הטוב שבתרגום וכמבפ"נ, תרועה הוא כנגד בחי' מה שמעלין הטוב שבתרגום ללה"ק ומפילין הרע שבו שעי"ז ממילא נופל ונתבטל הרע של כל השבעים לשון ושם עיקר המלחמה, וזה בחי' תרועת מלחמה כ"ש וכי תבואו מלחמה בארצכם וכו' והרעותם וכו' וכמובא גם בזוה"ק ומחמת שיש בענין זה כמה בחינות ובכלל הם שני בחינות כי יש שהוא בבחינת ומדריגת עולם העשיה ששם הרע מרוב על הטוב, ויש שהוא בבחינת ומדריגת עולם היצירה ששם הרע והטוב על משקל אחד, ויש שהוא גבוה במדריגה עוד יותר והטוב שבו מרובה של הרע אך אעפי"כ גם אלו מריכין להתאנח הרבה לפני השי"ת עד שזוכיןלהפיל ולבטל הרע לגמרי ולהעלות הטוב למקומו, וזהבחי' שברים גנוחי גנח, אך אותם שהם בבחי' עשיה והרע שבהם מרובה על הטוב ובפרט אם כבר נכשלו ח"ו ע"י הרע שבהם הם צריכין לייליל ולצעוק בקולות מרות ותכופות מאד עד שיזכו לצאת ממה שצריכין לצאת ולתקן הכל בשלימות, וזה בחי' תרועה יילולי ייליל וכן אמרי רז"ל ומובא בספר ברית כהונת עולם ג"כ כי שברים ותרועה הם כנגד יצירה ועשיה, ומחמת שעפ"י רוב יש בכל אחד משני הבחינות הנ"ל כי יש מדות כאלה שהרע והטוב הם אצלו במשקל אחד ויש מדות שהוא כרוך אחריהם ביותר עד שהרע מרובה על הטוב ע"כ תקנו לתקוע שברים ותרועה ביחד ג"כ, נמצא ששברים ותרועה הם להעלות הטוב שבתרגום ללה"ק כנ"ל, וזה בחי' תקיעה שלאחריה היינו כנגד בחי' הלה"ק שיש לו שלימות יותר ע"י שהעלו גם הטוב שבתרגום לתוכו כנ"ל וע"כ אמרו רז"ל תקיעת שופר חכמה כי הוא כנגד בחי' אשה חכמה בחי' לה"ק המבפ"נ וזה ג"כ בחי' הג' ספרים הנ"ל רשעים גמורים הם בחי' אשת כסילות שהוא כלליות הרע של השבעים לשון, צדיקים גמורים הם בבחי' אשה חכמה בחי' חכמת נשים בחי' לשון הקודש, בינונים הם בבחי' האשה משכלת שהיא כנגד בחי'תרגום כמבפ"נ, וזה שמובא כיתרועה אותיות תורה עי"ן כי ע"י התרועה מפילין הרעע שבתרגום וממילא נופל הרע של כעל הע' אומות ועי"ז זוכין לע' פנים של תורה וכמבואר במ"א והם בבחי' שלימות לה"ק ע"י לשון תרוגם שזה בחי' שלימות תורה שבכתב ע"י תורה שבע"פ וכמובן בפנים. ומחמת שזה סוד כוונת המילה כמבפ"נ ע"כ מלין קודם לתקיעת שופר כמבואר בשו"ע כי בזה שחותכין הערלהופריעה עי"ז מפילין הרע של הע' לשון בפועל ממש וממשיכין בחי' תיקון הברית ושלימות לה"ק שזה כל ענין תקיעת שופר כנ"ל:
units.en:
This is the dimension of the Three Books opened on Rosh HaShanah — specifically books, for a book serves remembrance, which is in the power of imagination, the dimension of Targum, as explained in the main text.

The completely righteous — who have merited to elevate even the good within Targum to the Holy Tongue, so that evil has no foothold in them — are certainly inscribed immediately for life.

The completely wicked are of the dimension of the complete evil of the seventy tongues. They seek to prevail and to draw sustenance even from holiness, heaven forbid, through the evil within Targum. But holiness overpowers them and casts them down through the dimension of the flame of fire explained in the main text. Therefore they are immediately inscribed for death, may G-d protect us.

The intermediate ones are those of the dimension of good and evil, the dimension of Targum, who have not yet merited to elevate the good within Targum and cast down the evil within it. Therefore they remain suspended until Yom Kippur. Through repentance during the Ten Days of Repentance, they merit to rectify the language of Targum as well, until they too are inscribed for life.

This is the dimension of Tekia, Teruah, Tekia. The Tekia before corresponds to the dimension of the speech of the Holy Tongue coming from above, which still lacks rectification, for the good within Targum must be elevated, as explained in the main text.

Teruah corresponds to elevating the good within Targum to the Holy Tongue and casting down the evil within it, through which the evil of all seventy tongues consequently falls and is nullified. There lies the principal battle, the dimension of the Teruah of war, as it is written, "And when you come to war in your land," etc., "and you shall sound the Teruah," etc., as is also brought in the holy Zohar.

Because this matter has several dimensions, which in general comprise two kinds: one person is in the dimension and level of the World of Asiyah, where evil exceeds good; another is in the dimension and level of the World of Yetzirah, where evil and good are balanced equally. Another is at an even higher level, where the good within him exceeds the evil. Nevertheless, even those at the higher level must sigh extensively before G-d, Yisburach, until they merit to cast down and nullify the evil completely and elevate the good to its proper place.

This is the dimension of Sh'vorim, "groaning."

Those who are in the dimension of Asiyah, however, where the evil within them exceeds the good — especially if they have already stumbled, heaven forbid, through the evil within them — must wail and cry out with exceedingly bitter and rapid cries until they merit to emerge from whatever they must emerge from and rectify everything in completeness. This is the dimension of Teruah, "wailing."

Our Sages, z"l, likewise taught, and it is also brought in the book Bris Kehunas Olam, that Sh'vorim and Teruah correspond to Yetzirah and Asiyah.

Since most people possess both of the above dimensions — there are qualities in which evil and good are equally balanced within them, and there are other qualities after which they are especially drawn, so that evil exceeds good — the Sages therefore instituted sounding Sh'vorim and Teruah together as well.

Thus Sh'vorim and Teruah are for elevating the good within Targum to the Holy Tongue, as explained above.

The Tekia after corresponds to the Holy Tongue, which attains greater completeness because the good within Targum has also been elevated into it, as above.

Therefore our Sages, z"l, said, "Sounding the Shofar is wisdom," for it corresponds to the wise woman, the dimension of the Holy Tongue, as explained in the main text.

This is also the dimension of the Three Books mentioned above. The completely wicked correspond to the foolish woman, the totality of the evil of the seventy tongues. The completely righteous correspond to the wise woman, the dimension of the wisdom of women, the Holy Tongue. The intermediate ones correspond to the understanding woman, who corresponds to the dimension of Targum, as explained in the main text.

This is what is brought concerning Teruah containing the letters Torah and Ayin, for through Teruah one casts down the evil within Targum, and consequently the evil of all seventy nations falls. Through this one merits the seventy faces of Torah, as explained elsewhere. These correspond to the completeness of the Holy Tongue through Targum, the dimension of the Written Torah being brought to completeness through the Oral Torah, as may be understood from the main text.

Because this is the secret of the intention of circumcision, as explained in the main text, one therefore performs a circumcision before sounding the Shofar, as explained in the Shulchan Aruch. For through cutting away the foreskin and performing priah, one actually casts down the evil of the seventy tongues and draws down the rectification of the covenant and the completeness of the Holy Tongue, which is the entire matter of Shofar-sounding, as explained above.

history.earlier_supplied_English:
The world was created in the Holy Tongue (Lashon HaKodesh), which is the dimension of Chava (Eve) — woman — Malchus. Therefore on every Rosh HaShanah Israel engage in building Malchus — the dimension of the completeness of the Holy Tongue.

Just as at the beginning of creation it is written: "and G-d cast a deep sleep upon the man" — the dimension of Targum (translation/earthly speech) — so every year one must draw this dimension to elevate the good within Targum into the Holy Tongue. And just as the serpent came and enticed Chava — so every Rosh HaShanah the serpent — the dimension of the totality of evil of the seventy nations — intensifies and all the princes of the nations accuse and seek to sever the sacred union.

Therefore G-d commanded us to sound the Shofar — to awaken the merit of Yaakov.

qualifications.text: The source uses books specifically because remembrance is linked with imagination and Targum. It distinguishes the immediately inscribed righteous and wicked from intermediate persons whose mixed condition can be rectified through repentance by Yom Kippur.

The source connects the initial Tekia with the Holy Tongue before its completion, Teruah with the battle to raise good from Targum and eliminate evil, and the final Tekia with the Holy Tongue made more complete by that elevation.

Although the source announces two general kinds of inner struggle, it also names a third, higher level with more good than evil. Those at the higher level still require groaning, while the Asiyah level, especially after wrongdoing, requires intense wailing. A person can have different qualities corresponding to both primary conditions.

The source associates Sh'vorim with Yetzirah and Teruah with Asiyah and names Bris Kehunas Olam. It then associates the Three Books with the foolish woman, wise woman and understanding woman respectively; no additional book title or halachic locator is supplied.

The Teruah association combines Torah with the letter Ayin and connects the fall of the seventy nations' evil to the seventy faces of Torah. The fully spelled letter name עי"ן is not asserted to be a literal additional word that can be permuted with תורה into תרועה.

The concluding circumcision discussion specifically includes cutting the foreskin and priah before Shofar-sounding, connecting both with the covenant and the completeness of the Holy Tongue. It is not a general claim that circumcision is invariably performed on Rosh HaShanah.

units.he: וזה בחי' מלכיות זכרונות ושופרות, מלכיות הוא בחי'מלכות פה בחי' שלימות לה"ק וע"כ משבחין שם את השי"ת מאד שלא עשנו כגויי הארצות וכו' כי השי"ת בחר בנו מכל עם ורוממנו מכל לשון וכמבפ"נ, זכרונות הוא כנגד בחי' תיקון הברית בבחי' יזכור לעולם בריתו וגם מזכירין שם עיקדת יצחק שעי"ז המתיק הגבורות בשרשן וכלל שמאלא בימינא כמבואר בזוה"ק ועי"ז נשלם בחי' היראה שהוא מדת יצחק וע"י היראה עיקר התיקון של לשון הקודש כנ"ל, גם עי"ז נמשך התיקון שיכולין אנחנו לזכות להעלות הטוב שבתרגום ללה"ק שזה ג"כ בחי' לאכללא שמאלא בימינא, וע"כ תיכף אחר העקידה נתבשר יצחק שנולד זיווגו בפדן אדם דיקא כי זכה לברר הטוב שבארם שהוא בחי' תרגום, וע"כ דקדשה התרוה לספר שרבקה היתה מפדן ארם בת בתואל הארמי ואחות לבן הארמי ואעפי"כ זכתה הצדקת הזאת ונתדבקה ביצחק שהוא עולה תמימה בחי' לה"ק, ומחמת שכ"ז ממשיכין עכשיו ע"י שופר ע"כ אומרים ברכת שופרות ומזכירין שם פסוקי שופר של מתן תורה כנ"ל ופסוקי שופר של לעתיד שעי"ז נזכה לחירות עולם ולצאת מהגלות של שבעים לשון ולהפיל הרע שבהם ולהכניעו לגמרי, וע"כ נהגו כל ישראל להתפלל בערב ר"ה על קברי צדייקם שזה בחי' תיקון הברית כמבואר במ"א והתפלה שמתפללין שם מקובלת מאד כי היא בבחי' שלימות לשון הקודש שתלוי בתיקון הברית כמבפ"נ:
units.en:
This is the dimension of Malchuyos, Zichronos and Shofaros.

Malchuyos is the dimension of Malchus-mouth, the dimension of the completeness of the Holy Tongue. Therefore one greatly praises G-d, Yisburach, there, that He did not make us like the nations of the lands, etc., for G-d, Yisburach, chose us from every people and exalted us above every tongue, as explained in the main text.

Zichronos corresponds to the dimension of rectifying the covenant, in the dimension of "He shall remember His covenant forever." One also mentions there the Binding of Yitzchok, through which the severities were sweetened at their root and the left was included within the right, as explained in the holy Zohar. Through this the dimension of awe, the quality of Yitzchok, was completed, and through awe the principal rectification of the Holy Tongue is accomplished, as explained above.

Through this one also draws down the rectification by which we can merit to elevate the good within Targum to the Holy Tongue. This too is the dimension of including the left within the right.

Therefore immediately after the Binding, Yitzchok received news that his destined mate had been born specifically in Paddan Aram, for he merited to clarify the good within Aram, the dimension of Targum.

Therefore the Torah was particular to relate that Rivka was from Paddan Aram, the daughter of Besuel the Aramean and the sister of Lavan the Aramean. Nevertheless, this righteous woman merited to cleave to Yitzchok, who was a perfect burnt offering, the dimension of the Holy Tongue.

Because all this is now drawn down through the Shofar, one therefore recites the blessing of Shofaros, mentioning there the Shofar verses concerning the Giving of the Torah, as above, and the Shofar verses of the future. Through this we shall merit everlasting freedom, emergence from the exile of the seventy tongues, and the complete casting down and subjugation of their evil.

Therefore all Israel customarily pray at the graves of Tzadikim on Erev Rosh HaShanah. This is the dimension of rectifying the covenant, as explained elsewhere. The prayer offered there is exceedingly accepted, for it is in the dimension of the completeness of the Holy Tongue, which depends upon rectifying the covenant, as explained in the main text.

history.earlier_supplied_English: For Yaakov merited to humble the serpent and was in the house of Lavan the Aramean, and clarified the good within Targum and elevated it to the Holy Tongue.

qualifications.text: Malchuyos is connected with Malchus-mouth and the Holy Tongue; Zichronos is connected with the covenant and the Binding of Yitzchok. Including the left within the right is associated with sweetening severities, completing awe and raising the good within Targum.

The supplied location פדן אדם says Paddan Adam, whereas the repeated context of Aram, Targum, Besuel and Lavan supports a contextual Paddan Aram reading. The source wording is unchanged, and this is not a claim of original-print correction.

The passage connects Rivka's Aramean family and birthplace with her eventual attachment to Yitzchok, described as a perfect burnt offering. It does not assert that Yitzchok physically died at the Binding.

The closing custom of praying at the graves of Tzadikim on Erev Rosh HaShanah is connected specifically to covenantal rectification and the acceptance of prayer through the Holy Tongue, not to a newly supplied external reference.

units.he: ואחר ראש השנה עוסקין בתשובה שעי"ז מעלין את הטוב שבתרגום ומפילין הרע שבו ומשלימין את לה"ק עד שזוכין ליו"כ ואז המלכות שהיא בחי'לה"ק נשלמת באור גדול וניזונית רק מבחי' קולות הפנימיים שהם בחי' החמשה תפלות של יו"כ שהם בבחי' שלימות לה"ק ואז נופלת כל הרע של כל השבעים לשון וכן הרע שבתרגום וישראל זוכין לסליחת עוונות כי כל העוונות באים רק מהרע הנ"ל והשטן בעצמו מעיד אז על ישראל שהם דומים למלאכי השרת ומלאכי השרת הם בבחי' לשון הקודש כי אין נזקקין ללשון תרגום כמו שאז"ל (שבת דף י"ב ע,ש ובשו"ע סי' ק"ע) וזה בחי' כי גדול יום ה' ונורא מאד ומני יכילנו זה יו"כ (עיין תנחומא פ' וישלח) כי אז היראה גדולה מאד שעי"ז נשלם הלה"ק כי רב מאד מחנהו אלו המלאכים שמלמדין זכות וחובה כי עצום עושי דברו כי ישראל הם אז עושי דברו דעבדין להאי דבר כי משלימין את הלה"ק ובונים כביכול הדיבור של הקב"ה בשלימות ועי"ז זוכין לסליחת עוונות וע"כ מתוודין אז הרבה בפה מלא בכדי לתקן כל הפגמים שפגמו ע"י העוונות באותיות הדבירו של לה"ק וע"י התשובה והוידוים בבחי' קחו עמכם דברים וכו' מתקנין זאת:
units.en:
After Rosh HaShanah one engages in repentance, through which the good within Targum is elevated, its evil is cast down and the Holy Tongue is brought to completeness, until one merits Yom Kippur.

Then Malchus, the dimension of the Holy Tongue, is completed with great illumination and is nourished only from the dimension of the inner voices, which are the dimension of the five prayers of Yom Kippur, themselves in the dimension of the completeness of the Holy Tongue.

Then all the evil of all seventy tongues falls, as does the evil within Targum. Israel merits forgiveness of sins, for all sins arise only from the evil mentioned above.

The Accuser himself then testifies concerning Israel that they resemble the ministering angels. The ministering angels are of the dimension of the Holy Tongue, for they do not attend to the language of Targum, as our Sages, z"l, said (Shabbos 12; see there and Shulchan Aruch, Siman 170).

This is the dimension of "For the day of G-d is great and exceedingly awesome; who can endure it?" — this is Yom Kippur (see Tanchuma, Parshas Vayishlach). For awe is then exceedingly great, through which the Holy Tongue is completed.

"For exceedingly great is His camp" — these are the angels who teach merit and liability. "For mighty are the doers of His word" — for Israel are then those who perform His word, who accomplish this speech, since they complete the Holy Tongue and build, as it were, the speech of the Blessed Holy One in completeness. Through this they merit forgiveness of sins.

Therefore one confesses extensively at that time with a full mouth, in order to rectify all the blemishes caused by sins in the letters of speech of the Holy Tongue. Through repentance and confessions, in the dimension of "Take words with you," etc., these blemishes are rectified.

history.earlier_supplied_English:
This is the dimension of the Separation of Rosh HaShanah — involving the "deep sleep," "and G-d built the rib" — all these rectifications must be drawn on every Rosh HaShanah.

The Shofar and the Two Sounds

The mitzvah of Shofar-sounding is the dimension of the awakening from sleep — for sleep and deep sleep are the dimension of Targum. One must awaken from the sleep — elevating the good within Targum to the Holy Tongue. And therefore one blesses: "to hear (lishmoah) the voice of the Shofar" — specifically hear — for Awe is tied to the ears. And this is: "G-d, I heard Your report, I was awed" [Hab. 3:2].

The Shofar is also called Shofar from the language of "improve your deeds" (shafru maasaychem) — from the language of Targum — for through this one elevates the good within Targum.

qualifications.text: The passage connects repentance with raising the good within Targum, eliminating its evil and completing the Holy Tongue. Yom Kippur's five prayers are identified with the inner voices nourishing Malchus.

The source gives שבת דף י"ב and שו"ע סי' ק"ע in connection with ministering angels and Targum. The English renders the literal Shulchan Aruch numeral ק"ע as 170, without silently replacing it with Orach Chayim 101:4. Shabbos 12b and that separate Shulchan Aruch passage provide contextual parallels, not an original-print correction or attestation of the complete cited sections.

The source distinguishes the Accuser's testimony that Israel resemble ministering angels from the angels' role as those who teach merit and liability. The supplied עושי דברו is plural and is retained as 'doers of His word'; the passage separately interprets Israel as those performing and completing divine speech.

The closing confessions are spoken with a full mouth to rectify blemishes caused by sin in the letters of the Holy Tongue. The abbreviated instruction 'Take words with you' is retained without adding an unprinted biblical continuation.

units.he: ואחר יו"כ נכנסין לסוכה והוא זכר להיקף ענני כבודש שהיו בבחי' שלימות לה"ק כ"ש בעמוד ענן ידבר אליהם גם הם בחי' שמירת הברית שמו שפירש"י על פסוק והוקע אותם לה' נגד השמש שאותם שנכשלו היה הענין נקפל מעליהם וע"כ נקראים ענני כבוד בחי' תיקון הברית ושלימות לה"ק שהם בחי' כבוד כמבפ"נ, וע"כ היו שואבין אז רוה"ק בשמחת בית השואבה כי לשון הקודש היא בחי' רוח הקודש כמבפ"נ, וזה בחי' תצפנם בסוכה מריב לשונות כי נצולים בזה מהרע של שבעים לשון, וע"כ מקריבין אז שבעים פרים כנגד השבעים לשון שמתמעטין והולכין וכו' כשארז"ל היינו שהרע שבהם נופל ונתבטל והטוב שינקו מבחי' לשון הקודש ע"י לשון תרגום נתברר מביניהם וחוזר ועלה לשרשו וע"כ לעתיד לבוא יהיה מפלת העכו"ם ע"י נסיון של מצוות סוכה כשארז"ל וע"כ מצות סוכה הוא אכילה ושתיה ושינה כי כל זה נתתקן אז ע"י בחי' סוכה, שינה היא בחי' תרדימה בחי' תרגום שהטוב שבו מתברר ועולה ללשון הקודש שהוא בחי' סוכה ועי"ז נתתקן האכילה ושתיה שתהיו בבחי' ויאכל וישת וייטב לבו שאכילתו ושתייתו יהי מהתנוצצות האותיות של מעשה בראשית שיש בכל דבר כמפב"נ, וזה בחי' לב שמח ייטיב פנים כמבפ"נ, וזה בחי' השמחה של סוכות:
units.en:
After Yom Kippur one enters the Sukka, which commemorates the encompassing Clouds of Glory. These were in the dimension of the completeness of the Holy Tongue, as it is written, "In a pillar of cloud He spoke to them."

They are also of the dimension of guarding the covenant, as may be understood from Rashi's explanation of the verse "And hang them before G-d, facing the sun": the cloud was folded back from those who had stumbled. Therefore they are called Clouds of Glory, the dimension of rectifying the covenant and completing the Holy Tongue, both of which are dimensions of honor, as explained in the main text.

Therefore at Simchas Bais HaShoaiva they drew the Holy Spirit, for the Holy Tongue is the dimension of the Holy Spirit, as explained in the main text.

This is the dimension of "You shall conceal them in a Sukka from the strife of tongues," for through this one is saved from the evil of the seventy tongues.

Therefore one offers seventy bulls at that time, corresponding to the seventy tongues, which progressively diminish, etc., as our Sages, z"l, taught. That is, the evil within them falls and is nullified, while the good that they had drawn from the dimension of the Holy Tongue through Targum is separated from among them and returns and ascends to its root.

Therefore in the future the downfall of the nations will come through the trial of the mitzvah of Sukka, as our Sages, z"l, taught.

Therefore the mitzvah of Sukka includes eating, drinking and sleeping, for all these are rectified then through the dimension of Sukka.

Sleep is the dimension of deep sleep, the dimension of Targum, from which the good is separated and ascends to the Holy Tongue, which is the dimension of Sukka.

Through this eating and drinking are rectified, so that they will be in the dimension of "And he ate and drank, and his heart was glad." That is, his eating and drinking will be from the sparkling illumination of the letters of the act of creation that are within everything, as explained in the main text.

This is the dimension of "A joyful heart makes the face good," as explained in the main text. And this is the dimension of the joy of Sukkos.

history.earlier_supplied_English: And this is: "fortunate is the people who know the Teruah; G-d, in the light of Your face they shall walk" — for through this one merits an illuminated face.

qualifications.text: The source identifies the Clouds of Glory with both the completeness of the Holy Tongue and guarding the covenant. Its explanation of the cloud withdrawing from offenders is attributed to Rashi in connection with והוקע אותם לה' נגד השמש.

The supplied Rashi-related wording הענין נקפל מעליהם is irregular. The surrounding discussion of the Clouds of Glory supports a contextual reading of the cloud being folded back from the offenders, without changing the Hebrew or claiming an original printed correction.

The seventy bulls correspond to the seventy tongues. The source distinguishes the fall of their evil from the recovery of the good that had drawn nourishment from the Holy Tongue through Targum and now returns to its root.
The future trial involving Sukka is presented as a teaching of the Sages. The text does not supply its complete narrative or an additional tractate reference.

The source connects sleeping in the Sukka with the rectification of Targum, then connects eating and drinking with illumination from the letters of creation within food and drink. The final joyful-heart and illuminated-face association leads directly to the joy of Sukkos.
The current English follows the Hebrew shown here. Earlier supplied English is kept separately for comparison.

units.he: וזה בחי' נטילת הד' מנים אתרוג דומה ללב ששם שורש הדיבור של לשון הקודש כי הלשו הוא קולמס הלב וזה בחי' חם לבי בקרבי וכו' דברתי בלשוני, גם היראה היא דבר המסור ללב, גם שמיעה בלבא תליא כ"ש ונתת לעבדך לב שומע וזה בחי' ה' שמעתי שמעך יראתי, לולב דומה לשדרה בחי' צדיק חי עלמין בחי', תיקון הברית, הדס דומה לעינים זה בחי' תקון השינה והתרדימה שהוא בעינים בחי' אל תתן שינה לעיניך ועוד הרבה כזה, וזה בחי' עליית הטוב שבתרגום ע"י תיקון השגגות שהמעשה רע וכוונתו טוב שזה בחי' הדס שיש לו ריח ואין לו טעם, ערבה דומה לפה זה בחי' הדיבור בעצמו של לשון הקודש, ורז"ל דרשו פרי עץ הדר זה אברהם וכו' כי אברהם הוא הראשון אחר דור ההפלגה שזכה ללה"ק וע"כ נקרא אברהם העברי שדיבר בלשון עבריות שהוא לשון הקודש ורק לו ולזרעו אחריו נשאר לשון זה, גם הוא הראשון שנצטווה על המילה שזה בחי' ביטול הרע של השבעים לשון, כפות תמרים זה יצחק שהוא בחי' יראה שעי"ז עיקר תיקון הלשון הקודש, ענף עץ עבות זה יעקב שזכה לבררהטוב שבתרגום ולהעלותו ללשון קודש כנ"ל, וערבי נחל זה יוסף שזכה לתיקון הברית בשלימות ולשלימות לשון הקודש והיה יודע לפשר חלמין שבתרדימה ע"י שהעלה את הטוב שבתרגום גם בא גבריאל ולמדו כל השבעים לשון כשארז"ל כי הוא זכה בשלימות להפיל כל הרע שבהם ולהעלות ניצוצי לשון הקודש שנפלו ביניהם, עוד יש לומד כי כל הארבע מינים אלו מרמזין על גודל מעלת הצדיק האמת, וזה בחי' פרי עץ הדר הוא בחי' הדיבור לשון הקודש של הצדיק בעצמו שהוא בחי' פרי צדיק עץ חיים ולו עיקר ההידור כי זוכה לבחי' פנים מאירות המובפ"נ, כפות תמרים מרמז על שהצדיק דומה לשדרה שהוא עיקר הבנין של קומת האדם כמו כן הצדיק הוא הבנין של כל המקורבים אלי וסובבים אותו ומקושרים אליו כמו העלין של הלולב להשדרה ועי"ז ממשיך עליהם ג"כ מקדושת והעליונה, ענף עך עבות דומה לעינים מרמז על מעלת קדושת ההסתכלות בפני הצדיק שעי"ז בעצמו יכולין להתעוראר בתשובה כמבפ"נ, ערבה דמה לפה מרמז על מעלת הזוכה לשמוע דברי תורה מפי הצדיק שעי"ז זוכה לקבל דיבור לשון הקודש בשלימות היינו ביראה כמבפ"נ:
units.en:
This is the dimension of taking the Four Species.

The esrog resembles the heart, where the speech of the Holy Tongue has its root, for the tongue is the pen of the heart. This is the dimension of "My heart grew warm within me," etc., "I spoke with my tongue."

Awe, too, is a matter entrusted to the heart. Hearing also depends upon the heart, as it is written, "And give Your servant a hearing heart." This is the dimension of "G-d, I heard Your report, I was awed."

The lulav resembles the spine, the dimension of the Tzadik, the Life of the Worlds, the dimension of rectifying the covenant.

The hadas resembles the eyes. This is the dimension of rectifying sleep and deep sleep, which are associated with the eyes, in the dimension of "Do not give sleep to your eyes," and many similar expressions.

This is the dimension of elevating the good within Targum through rectifying inadvertent transgressions, in which the deed is evil but the intention is good. This is the dimension of the hadas, which has fragrance but no taste.

The arova resembles the mouth. This is the dimension of the actual speech of the Holy Tongue.

Our Sages, z"l, expounded: "A fruit of a beautiful tree" — this is Avraham, etc. For Avraham was the first, after the Generation of the Dispersion, to merit the Holy Tongue. Therefore he was called Avraham the Hebrew, for he spoke the Hebrew language, which is the Holy Tongue. This language remained only with him and with his descendants after him.

He was also the first to be commanded concerning circumcision, which is the dimension of nullifying the evil of the seventy tongues.

"Branches of date palms" — this is Yitzchok, who is the dimension of awe, through which the principal rectification of the Holy Tongue is accomplished.

"A branch of a leafy tree" — this is Yaakov, who merited to clarify the good within Targum and elevate it to the Holy Tongue, as explained above.

"Willows of the brook" — this is Yosef, who merited complete rectification of the covenant and completeness of the Holy Tongue. He knew how to interpret dreams that occur during deep sleep, for he had elevated the good within Targum.

Gavriel also came and taught him all seventy languages, as our Sages, z"l, taught. For Yosef had merited completely to cast down all the evil within them and to elevate the sparks of the Holy Tongue that had fallen among them.

There is yet another way to explain this: all four of these species allude to the greatness of the true Tzadik.

"A fruit of a beautiful tree" is the dimension of the Tzadik's own speech in the Holy Tongue, in the dimension of "The fruit of a righteous person is a tree of life." The principal beauty belongs to him, for he merits the dimension of an illuminated face explained in the main text.

"Branches of date palms" alludes to the Tzadik resembling the spine, which is the principal support of the structure of the human being. Likewise, the Tzadik is the support of all those who draw near to him, surround him and are bound to him, just as the leaves of the lulav are attached to its spine. Through this he also draws down upon them his supernal holiness.

"A branch of a leafy tree" resembles the eyes, alluding to the great holiness of looking upon the face of the Tzadik. Through this alone one can be awakened to repentance, as explained in the main text.

The arova resembles the mouth, alluding to the great merit of one who hears words of Torah from the mouth of the Tzadik. Through this one merits to receive the speech of the Holy Tongue in completeness, namely, with awe, as explained in the main text.

history.earlier_supplied_English: And therefore fortunate is one who merits to come to the true Tzadik on Rosh HaShanah and to gaze upon his illuminated face — and all the more to merit hearing from his mouth some Torah teaching — through which one receives from him the speech of the Holy Tongue in completeness.

qualifications.text: The first Four Species interpretation associates the esrog with the heart as the root of speech, awe and hearing; the lulav with the Tzadik and covenant; the hadas with the eyes, sleep and inadvertent transgressions; and the arova with the actual speech of the Holy Tongue.
The designation צדיק חי עלמין is rendered as the Tzadik, the Life of the Worlds. No unsupported count of eighteen worlds is introduced.

The hadas is associated with an inadvertent transgression whose deed is wrong but whose intention is good. Its fragrance without taste represents this distinction, rather than a claim that all deeds accompanied by good intentions are permissible.

The second Four Species interpretation identifies Avraham with the Holy Tongue after the Generation of the Dispersion and with circumcision, Yitzchok with awe, Yaakov with elevating the good within Targum, and Yosef with covenantal rectification, dream interpretation and mastery of the seventy languages.

The third interpretation concerns the true Tzadik: his own holy speech and illuminated face, his support of attached followers, the spiritual effect of looking upon his face, and the merit of hearing Torah from his mouth. These are distinct from the earlier patriarchal correspondences.
The source attributes the teaching of the seventy languages to Gavriel and the interpretation of dreams to Yosef's raising the good from Targum. No additional narrative or source locator is supplied.

In the third Four Species interpretation, the source prints ענף עך עבות, rather than the earlier ענף עץ עבות, and prints ערבה דמה לפה, rather than the earlier patriarchal ערבי נחל. The English reads the branch contextually as 'a branch of a leafy tree' and retains the singular arova at the final correspondence, without changing the Hebrew. The Tzadik's followers are printed as מקורבים אלי, 'those who draw near to me,' although the surrounding סובבים אותו ומקושרים אליו refers to those surrounding and bound to him. The English follows that third-person context without claiming an original-print correction.
The current English follows the Hebrew shown here. Earlier supplied English is kept separately for comparison.

units.en: Passage beginning “And this is what our Sages, z"l, expounded”

history.earlier_supplied_English:
His disciples, z"l, accepted this upon themselves and agreed to do so every Rosh HaShanah.
And with G-d's help, this has already been [the practice] for more than sixty years*
after his passing, z"l —
and even so, the matter continues among the Anash [Breslov Chassidim]

qualifications.text: The supplied ד"ה וזה שדרז"ל is a partial discourse incipit only. The unrelated historical account of disciples and their practice is not imported.
The current English follows the Hebrew shown here. Earlier supplied English is kept separately for comparison.

units.he: וזה שדרז"ל שהמינים אלו מרמזין על כל הכתות שבישראל כי יש שיש להם טעם וריח כמו האתרוג זה בחי' הצדיקים שזוכין לשלימות לה"ק שהוא בחי' טעם כמו טעמו וראו שפירשו מלשון דיברו, וריח הוא בחי' יראה כ"ש והריחו ביראת ה', גם ריח הוא בחי'תיקון הברית כמובן בליקות"נ סימן ל"ב ובמעשה של יום השני מהז' בעטלירס, ויש שיש להם איזה בחי' מבחינת לה"ק היינו שעוסקים לדבר דיבורים קדושים לפני השי"ת בתורה ובתפלה אבל אין להם ריח כי לא זכו עדיין ליראה בשלימות, ויש שיש להם ריח שזכו לאיזה בחי' יראה ותיקון הברית אבל אין להם טעם כי מתרשלים בענין הדיבור של לה"ק, ויש שאין להם לא טעם ולא ריח כי רחוקים מכל הבחינות הנ"ל, אמר הקב"ה יעשו כולם אגודה אחת ויכפרו אלו על אלו כי ע"י הכלליות שנכללין ביחד בענין ההתקשרות וההתקרבות אל הצדיק עי"ז יכולן לקבל תיקון ושלימות ע"י כל הבחינות הנ"ל היינו ע"י ההתקרבות וההתקשרות לבד כי המחובר לטהור טהור וע"י ההסתכלות בפניו וע"י ששומעין מפיו תורה כנ"ל ועל כן אלו הג' מינים הם אגודה אחת כי כולם הם מסוג אחד מאחר שאין להם שלימות עדיין והאתרוג הוא בפני עצמו כי הוא מרמז על קדושת הדיבור של הצדיק שיש לו שלימות אמיתי והוא בסוג אחר לגמרי מהם אעפי"כ צריך הוא להיות סמוך וקרוב מאד אל הג' מינים ועי"ז כולם מקבלין שלימות כנ"ל, וע"כ האתרוג דייקא בשמאל והלולב ומיניו בימין כי צריך לאכללא שמאלא בימינא וימינא בשמאלא שזה סוד עיקדת יצחק שעי"ז נשתלשל עד שיכולין להעלות גם הטוב שבתרגום ללשון קודש שזה עיקר השלימות כנ", ומחמת שזה הצדיק מוריד א"ע אל המקורבים שיש בהם עדיין אחיזת טוב ורע בחי'תרגום שזה בחי' שהימין מוריד ומחבר עצמו אל בחי' שמאל ע"כ האתרוג בשמאל ומה שהמקורבים להוטים אחר הצדיק להתקרב אליו ולהכלל בו שזה בחי' לאכללא שמאלא בימינא ע"כ הג' מניים הם בימין וע"כ כשנוטלין זה אחר זה צריך ליטול גם את האתרוג בימין כמבואר בפסוקים, ומחמת שגם הצדיק מקבל תועלת גדול ע"י שמזכה את הרבים ומקרב אותם להשי"ת שזה בחי' שמעלה הטוב שבתרגום שעי"ז עיקר שלימות לה"ק כנ"ל ובחי' זאת מרומז העיקר בהלולב שהדר"ה שהוא בחי' הצדיק בחי' צדיק כתמר יפרח מכוסהבהעלין שהם בחי' המקרובים שלו ע"כ מברכין על נטילת לולב מחמת שהוא גבוה מכולם היינו כנ"ל כי הוא כולל כולם, ובזה יש לכוון קצת דברינו הנ"ל למה שמובן בכוונות ואין להאריך בזה וגם כי כמה פנים לתורה כידוע, וע"כ אסור לאכול קודם נטילת לולב כי עי"ז עיקר תיקון האכילה שתהיה בבחי' יסעדך ומציון כמבפ"נ, וזהו שארז"ל הנוטל לולב באגודו וכו' כאלו בנה מזבח והקריב עליו קרבן מזבח הוא בחי' מלכות בחי' הדיבור של לה"ק בחי' זבחו זבחי צדק וצדק מלכותא קדישא בחי' צדק תדברון (וזה בחי' ונשלמה פרים [שמקריבין על המזבח] שפתינו) והקרבנות מבהמות טהורות שהם מבחי' הטוב שבנוגה זה בחי' שמעלין הטוב שבתרגום ללשון הקודש, וע"כ מכפריו על השגגות שהם מבחי' תרגום כנ"ל:
units.en:
This is what our Sages, z"l, expounded: these species allude to all the groups within Israel.

Some have both taste and fragrance, like the esrog. This is the dimension of the Tzadikim who merit the completeness of the Holy Tongue, which is the dimension of taste, as in "Taste and see," which they interpreted in the sense of "Speak and see."

Fragrance is the dimension of awe, as it is written, "And he shall smell in the fear of G-d." Fragrance is also the dimension of rectifying the covenant, as may be understood from Likutay Moharan, Part II, Siman 32, and from the story of the second day of the Seven Beggars.

Some possess a certain dimension of the Holy Tongue — that is, they engage in speaking holy words before G-d, Yisburach, in Torah and prayer — but they have no fragrance, for they have not yet merited complete awe.

Others have fragrance: they have merited some dimension of awe and rectification of the covenant, but have no taste, for they are negligent concerning speech in the Holy Tongue.

Others have neither taste nor fragrance, for they are distant from all the dimensions mentioned above.

The Blessed Holy One said that they should all form one bound group and bring atonement for one another. For through their collective inclusion together in connection and closeness to the Tzadik, they can receive rectification and completeness through all the dimensions mentioned above.

That is, through closeness and connection alone, for one who is joined to the pure is pure; through looking upon his face; and through hearing Torah from his mouth, as explained above.

Therefore these three species form one bound group, for they all belong to one category, since they have not yet attained completeness.

The esrog, however, stands by itself, for it alludes to the holiness of the Tzadik's speech, which possesses true completeness. He belongs to an entirely different category from them. Nevertheless, it must be exceedingly near and close to the three species, and through this all receive completeness, as above.

Therefore the esrog specifically is in the left hand, while the lulav and its species are in the right, for one must include the left within the right and the right within the left. This is the secret of the Binding of Yitzchok, through which matters developed until one could elevate even the good within Targum to the Holy Tongue, which is the principal completeness, as explained above.

Because this Tzadik lowers himself toward those who have drawn near to him, who still have a foothold of good and evil, the dimension of Targum, this is the dimension of the right descending and joining itself to the left. Therefore the esrog is in the left hand.

And because those who have drawn near eagerly seek the Tzadik, to approach him and become included within him, which is the dimension of including the left within the right, the three species are therefore in the right hand.

Therefore, when taking them one after another, one must also take the esrog in the right hand, as explained in the cited rulings.

Because the Tzadik also receives great benefit through bringing merit to the many and drawing them near to G-d, Yisburach — which is the dimension of elevating the good within Targum, through which the principal completeness of the Holy Tongue is attained, as explained above — this dimension is principally alluded to by the lulav.

For the spine of the lulav, which is the dimension of the Tzadik, in the dimension of "A righteous person shall flourish like a palm tree," is covered by its leaves, which are the dimension of those who have drawn near to him.

Therefore one recites the blessing "concerning taking the lulav," because it is taller than all of them. That is, as explained above, it encompasses them all.

Through this one may align our explanations somewhat with what is understood from the Kavanos. There is no need to elaborate here, particularly since the Torah has many interpretations, as is known.

Therefore it is forbidden to eat before taking the lulav, for through this comes the principal rectification of eating, so that it should be in the dimension of "May He sustain you, and from Tzion," as explained in the main text.

This is what our Sages, z"l, said: "One who takes a lulav in its bound group," etc., "is considered as though he built an altar and offered a sacrifice upon it."

The altar is the dimension of Malchus, the dimension of the speech of the Holy Tongue, in the dimension of "Offer sacrifices of righteousness." And righteousness, Tzedek, is holy Malchus, in the dimension of "You shall speak righteousness."

This is the dimension of "And we shall render bulls [which are offered upon the altar] with our lips."

The sacrifices are brought from pure animals, which are of the dimension of the good within Nogah. This is the dimension of elevating the good within Targum to the Holy Tongue. Therefore the sacrifices bring atonement for inadvertent transgressions, which are of the dimension of Targum, as explained above.

history.earlier_supplied_English:
Sh'mini Atzeres — The Holy Tongue Is Perfected

On Sh'mini Atzeres — the dimension of Malchus — the union of the Matron in completeness — for the speech of the Holy Tongue is perfected in completeness.

qualifications.text: The source distinguishes four groups: taste and fragrance together; holy speech without complete awe; awe or covenantal rectification without sufficient holy speech; and neither. Its account includes both Torah and prayer as holy speech.

The supplied reference names Likutay Moharan, Part II, Siman 32, and the second day of the Seven Beggars in connection with fragrance and covenantal rectification. No additional chapter or paragraph is supplied.

The three bundled species represent the still-incomplete groups, whereas the separate esrog represents the Tzadik's complete holy speech. Their required closeness is associated with mutual atonement through connection, looking upon the Tzadik and hearing Torah from him.

The esrog in the left hand and the three species in the right symbolize reciprocal inclusion of left and right. The source specifically distinguishes the Tzadik descending toward followers from followers seeking inclusion within the Tzadik.

The supplied כמבואר בפסוקים is literally 'as explained in the verses,' although its immediate context concerns the procedure for taking the esrog successively in the right hand and may point contextually to rulings. The English reflects that legal context without changing the Hebrew or claiming an original printed correction.

The Tzadik is described as benefiting from drawing others near, and the lulav's covering leaves symbolize his followers. The source connects the blessing on the tallest species with its encompassing the others, while explicitly leaving room for other Torah interpretations.
The printed יסעדך ומציון is retained as the abbreviated fragment 'May He sustain you, and from Tzion.' The English does not silently replace the conjunction or order with a canonical completed verse.

In ונשלמה פרים [שמקריבין על המזבח] שפתינו, the bracketed description qualifies the bulls offered upon the altar, not the lips. The sacrifice analogy links the altar with Malchus and holy speech, and pure animal offerings with elevating the good within Nogah and Targum.

The supplied שהדר"ה in the lulav passage is irregular. The preceding lulav-and-spine correspondence supports reading the physical spine or shaft of the lulav as the Tzadik, with the surrounding leaves representing those attached to him. The English retains this contextual relationship without emending שהדר"ה or claiming an original printed correction.
The current English follows the Hebrew shown here. Earlier supplied English is kept separately for comparison.

units.he: ד"ה וע"כ אומרים
units.en: Passage beginning “And therefore one says”

history.earlier_supplied_English:
Therefore I set my heart to examine his discourses, z"l,
and to search within them —
perhaps I would find some allusions (rmazim) to the topic of Rosh HaShanah in each of his discourses.
And with G-d's help, I found some allusions in most of his discourses, z"l, to the topic of Rosh HaShanah.

qualifications.text: The supplied ד"ה וע"כ אומרים is a partial discourse incipit. The unrelated historical first-person account of examining discourses is excluded.
The current English follows the Hebrew shown here. Earlier supplied English is kept separately for comparison.

units.he: וע"כ אומרים עם הד' מינים את הלל שהוא בחי' שלימות לה"ק כי עיקר שלימות הדיבור לדבר בו שבחו ית' ולהודות ולהלל לה' וכמבואר במ"א, וע"כ מנענעין בהודו לה' ובאנא ה' הושיעה נא כי בענין זה להשלים הלשון קודש ע"י הטוב שבתרגום בזה צריכין לעסוק לעולם ובכל פעם שממשיכין איזה תיקון ושלימות לה"ק צריכין להיות מודה על העבר וצועק לעתיד לבוא עד גמר התיקון ואעפי"כ צריכין לסיים בהודאה שזה בחי' הודו שבסוף ההלל כי צריכין לאכללא שמאלא בימינא כנ"ל:
units.en:
Therefore one recites Hallel with the Four Species, for Hallel is the dimension of the completeness of the Holy Tongue. The principal completeness of speech is to use it to speak His praise, Yisburach, and to thank and praise G-d, as explained elsewhere.

Therefore one waves the species at "Give thanks to G-d" and at "Please, G-d, save now."

For one must engage forever in this matter of bringing the Holy Tongue to completeness through the good within Targum. Each time one draws down some rectification and completeness of the Holy Tongue, one must give thanks for the past and cry out concerning the future, until the rectification is completed.

Nevertheless, one must conclude with thanksgiving, which is the dimension of "Give thanks" at the end of Hallel, for one must include the left within the right, as explained above.

history.earlier_supplied_English: And then all the nations fall — the evil of all seventy tongues collapses. And Israel remain in perfect isolation, cleaving to G-d in complete sacred unity, with no thing and no screen separating them.

qualifications.text: The source links Hallel to complete holy speech through praise and thanksgiving, and separately identifies waving the species at הודו לה' and אנא ה' הושיעה נא.
The rectification of the Holy Tongue is described as continuing: after each advance one thanks G-d for what has been accomplished and cries out for what remains, until completion.
The concluding thanksgiving is explicitly associated with the final הודו in Hallel and with including the left within the right; it does not cancel the preceding petition for future rectification.
The current English follows the Hebrew shown here. Earlier supplied English is kept separately for comparison.

units.he: ד"ה ואחר כל
units.en: Passage beginning “And after all”

history.earlier_supplied_English:
As is understood in the holy Zohar and in the intentions (kavanos) of the Ar"i z"l:
all the rectifications that are accomplished from Rosh HaShanah
until after Sh'mini Atzeres are all bound and interwoven with one another.
Because of this, I have mostly alluded within them also to the topic of Yom Kippur, Sukkos, and Sh'mini Atzeres.

qualifications.text: The supplied ד"ה ואחר כל is a partial discourse incipit. The historical account of the interconnected festival rectifications is not incorporated into this heading.
The current English follows the Hebrew shown here. Earlier supplied English is kept separately for comparison.

units.he: ואחר כל זה זוכין לשמיני עצרת שהוא בחי' מלכות בחי' זה יעצור בעמי כמבוראר בזוה"ק ואז זיווגא דמטרוניתא בשלימות כי נשלם הדיבור של לה"ק בשלימות עד שעי"ז נופלין כל הלשונות וישכון ישראל בטח בדד וכו' בחי' הן לבדד ישכון ורק הם זוכין לדבק עצמן בהשי"ת בשלימות ביחודא שלים ואין שום דבר ושום מסך המבדיל שיפרדי ח"ו היחוד והקשר שביניהם ואז הנוקבא עוצרת הטיפה שלא תפיל שמזה נמשך ונשתלשל גם למטה שע,י שלימות לה"ק ניצולין ממקה לילה ח"ו כמבפ"נ (עיין בליקוטי תניינא במאמר תקעו אמונה סי' ה'), וע,כ כל ישראל עולין אז לתורה שהוא עיקר שלימות לה"ק בחי' שנים מקרא וכו' ומסיימין ולכל המורא הגדול אשר עשה משה לעיני כל ישראל, וע"י היראה מעלין הטוב שבתרגום ומשלימין את הלה"ק ומביאין הארה והתנוצצות חדש בהאותיות שבכל מעשה בראשית וע"כ מתחילין תיכף במעשה בראשית בראשית ברא אלהים וכו' (וע"כ אז השמחה גדולה מאד בבחי' לב שמח ייטיב פנים כמבפ"נוכנ"ל לענין השמחה של סוכות ויעקב הוא אז רישא לחדוותא כי הוא זכה לברר הטוב שבתרגום ולהעלותו לשלימות לה"ק כמבפ"נ וכנ"ל):
units.en:
After all this one merits Sh'mini Atzeres, which is the dimension of Malchus, the dimension of "This one shall rule over My people," as explained in the holy Zohar.

On Sh'mini Atzeres — the dimension of Malchus — the union of the Matron is accomplished in completeness, for the speech of the Holy Tongue is perfected in completeness.

And then all the tongues fall — the evil of all seventy tongues collapses.

This is the dimension of "And Israel shall dwell securely, alone," etc., and the dimension of "Behold, alone he shall dwell." And only Israel merit to remain in perfect isolation, cleaving to G-d, Yisburach, in complete sacred unity, with no thing and no intervening screen separating, heaven forbid, the union and connection between them.

Then the feminine aspect retains the drop so that it does not fall. From this it also develops below that through the completeness of the Holy Tongue one is saved from a nocturnal emission, heaven forbid, as explained in the main text. See Likutay Moharan, Part II, in the discourse תקעו אמונה, Siman 5.

And therefore all Israel ascend to the Torah — the essential completeness of the Holy Tongue, the dimension of "twice Scripture," etc. — and one concludes: "and all the great Awe which Moshe performed before the eyes of all Israel" — for through Awe the good within Targum is elevated and the Holy Tongue is perfected.

Through this one brings new illumination and sparkling to the letters within the entire act of creation. Therefore one immediately begins the account of creation, "בראשית ברא אלהים," etc.

Therefore the joy at that time is exceedingly great, in the dimension of "A joyful heart makes the face good," as explained in the main text and as explained above concerning the joy of Sukkos.

And Yaakov is then the head of joy, for he merited to clarify the good within Targum and elevate it to the completeness of the Holy Tongue, as explained in the main text and above.

history.earlier_supplied_English: The Shofar and Drawing the Supernal Mental Faculties

qualifications.text: The source associates Sh'mini Atzeres with Malchus, the complete union of the Matron and the completion of the Holy Tongue. The quoted expression זה יעצור בעמי is connected with kingship and rule without expanding its wording.

The source states that all the tongues fall and that Israel remain securely alone in complete attachment to G-d, without a separating screen. This is distinct from an additional claim that every nation physically ceases to exist.

The account of the feminine aspect retaining the drop is connected with preventing a nocturnal emission below. The supplied ממקה לילה is irregular and is read contextually through מקרה לילה; no bodily miscarriage or change to the Hebrew is asserted.
The source explicitly directs the reader to Likutay Moharan, Part II, the discourse תקעו אמונה, Siman 5. No paragraph or subsection is supplied.

The Torah conclusion associates great awe with raising the good within Targum, completing the Holy Tongue and bringing renewed illumination to the letters of creation. The subsequent opening בראשית ברא אלהים is retained only to the extent supplied.

The concluding parenthetical connects Sh'mini Atzeres joy with the joyful-heart and illuminated-face correspondence discussed for Sukkos and identifies Yaakov as the head of joy because of his rectification of Targum.
The current English follows the Hebrew shown here. Earlier supplied English is kept separately for comparison.

units.he: ד"ה שייך לעיל
units.en: Passage beginning “Pertaining to the foregoing”

history.earlier_supplied_English:
Because of the great smallness of my understanding,
I am far from grasping this —
and would that I merit to understand at least the plain meaning of his holy words, z"l.
Therefore I have abbreviated in all these matters as much as possible,
and have come here only to mention and to arouse the heart of the reader
to search through each of his discourses, z"l,
regarding the holiness of Rosh HaShanah, etc. —
and certainly one whose understanding is truly broad,
who sets his mind and heart to these matters,
will find therein many wonders.
And this shall be my reward —
that I have begun to walk on this path —
even if it is not in my power to complete the matter as is fitting.

units.he: שייך לעיל לענין סוכה, וזה שמובא בזוה"ק כי סוכה אותיות כ"ו ה"ס בחי' יחוד השני שמות הק' הוי"ה אדנ"י שהם בחי' מחשבה ודיבור שזה בחי' שלימות הדיבור שהוא בחי' לשה"ק כשהדיבור ביחוד עם המחשבה שבלב, וע"כ דרז"ל במד"ר כי פי המדבר אליכם בלה"ק, ובמס' מגילה דף ט"ז ע"ב דרשו ע"ז כפי כן לבי וכמובא בסי' ל"ד, ובאמת שני הדרשות עולים בקנה אחד כי בחי' וכפי כן לבי שייך ג"כ לשלימות לה"ק כנ"ל, וזה בעצמו בחי' סוכה עילאה בחי' בינה לבא סוכה תתאה שהיא בחי' סוכת דוד בחי' מלכות פה המובא בזוה"ק, וענין זה שייך בהדרוש הזה בכמה מקומות הן לענין יו"כ שאז אימא וברתא יתיבין כחדא, וכן לענין מה שארז"ל אתרוג דומה ללב ועוד בשאר מקומות כמובן למעיין:
units.en:
This pertains to the foregoing discussion concerning Sukka.

This is what is brought in the holy Zohar: the letters of Sukka are כ"ו ה"ס, the dimension of the unification of the two holy Names, הוי"ה and אדנ"י. These are the dimensions of thought and speech, which is the dimension of the completeness of speech, the Holy Tongue, when speech is in union with the thought within the heart.

Therefore our Sages, z"l, expounded in Midrash Rabbah concerning "For it is my mouth speaking to you" — that he spoke in the Holy Tongue.

And in Megillah, page 16b, they expounded concerning this: "As my mouth, so is my heart," as brought in Siman 34.

In truth, the two interpretations amount to one, for the dimension of "As my mouth, so is my heart" likewise pertains to the completeness of the Holy Tongue, as explained above.

This itself is the dimension of the Supernal Sukka, the dimension of Bina, the heart; and the Lower Sukka, which is the dimension of the Sukka of David, the dimension of Malchus-mouth, as brought in the holy Zohar.

This matter pertains to several places in this discourse: both concerning Yom Kippur, when Ima and her daughter dwell together, and concerning what our Sages, z"l, said, that the esrog resembles the heart, and in other places, as may be understood by one who studies the matter.

history.earlier_supplied_English:
And therefore all Israel ascend to the Torah — the essential completeness of the Holy Tongue — and one concludes: "and all the great Awe which Moshe performed before the eyes of all Israel" — for through Awe the good within Targum is elevated and the Holy Tongue is perfected.

Translator's Summary — Siman 21

And immediately one begins Bereishis bara Elokim — the final letters spell Emes (Truth) — and the Messiah's spirit which will complete all rectifications and bring a new illumination to all the letters of the speech of creation.

Translator's Summary — Siman 19
Siman 19 reveals Rosh HaShanah's deepest linguistic secret: the Holy Tongue (Lashon HaKodesh) is the very substance of Malchus, and the seventy nations' tongues (the Targum) are both the raw material and the danger.

The work of Tishray is to extract the good within earthly speech and elevate it back to holy speech.

The Shofar awakens from the "sleep" of Targum. The Four Species map the Patriarchs to the dimensions of the Holy Tongue. Sh'mini Atzeres = the Holy Tongue's perfection = the fall of all seventy evil tongues forever.

On Rosh HaShanah We Engage in Building the Structure of the Divine Presence

Charity and the Mitzvah of Circumcision — Before the Shofar

The Three Blessings — Malchuyos, Zichronos, Shofaros

Sukkos and Sh'mini Atzeres

Translator's Summary — Siman 23 (and Conclusion)

qualifications.text: The opening שייך לעיל לענין סוכה is an explicit reference back to the earlier Sukka discussion. This owner remains substantive prose rather than a second heading or a translator's summary.

The supplied כ"ו ה"ס represents the numerical values 26 and 65 associated with the holy Names הוי"ה and אדנ"י. In this discourse their union is expressly interpreted as thought and speech, not thought and deed.

The passage attributes the Holy Tongue interpretation of כי פי המדבר אליכם to Midrash Rabbah and the mouth-and-heart interpretation כפי כן לבי to Megillah 16b, also referring to Siman 34. No further passage number or unprinted continuation is introduced.
The two interpretations of the same expression are reconciled because complete speech in the Holy Tongue corresponds to speech united with thought in the heart.

The source distinguishes the Supernal Sukka, Bina and heart, from the Lower Sukka, Davidic kingship and Malchus-mouth. It explicitly applies the correspondence to Yom Kippur's Ima-and-daughter union, the esrog-heart teaching and other locations in the same discourse.
The current English follows the Hebrew shown here. Earlier supplied English is kept separately for comparison.

history.earlier_supplied_English:
The Book Yerech HaAisonim — in it are explained many wondrous matters from the topic of
the holiness of Rosh HaShanah and the sounding of the Shofar and the prayers of Rosh HaShanah,
and the great merit of one who is privileged to be near a true Tzadik on Rosh HaShanah,
and the topic of the custom that was practiced to go on Erev Rosh HaShanah to pray at the graves of the Tzadikim;
and likewise explained within it are the topics of the holiness of the Ten Days of Repentance,
Yom Kippur, Sukkos, Sh'mini Atzeres, and Simchas Torah, and the holiness of all the mitzvos
of G-d which are observed during them.
